title: Topic 6 · 决策 — 神经科学

questions.question: 一只猴子已经学会「铃一响就有果汁」。某次铃响了，果汁却没有来。按奖励预测误差的理论，它的多巴胺神经元此刻会怎样？
options: 跌到基线以下，因为现实比预期差，差价为负
比平时爆发得更强，因为落空的意外让刺激更显著
保持不变，因为没有果汁就没有任何奖励信号
照常爆发，因为铃声已经带来了期待中的快乐
questions.explanation: 多巴胺报的是「现实 − 预期」的差价，不是快乐本身。学会预兆后爆发移到铃响那一刻；果汁按时到达时多巴胺不动，因为没有差价；预期落空时则跌破基线，像在说「亏了」。
questions.question_en: A monkey has learned that a bell means juice is coming. One time the bell rings but no juice arrives. Under reward prediction error theory, what do its dopamine neurons do at that moment?
options_en: Dip below baseline, because reality fell short of expectation and the error is negative
Burst more strongly than usual, because the surprise of the miss makes the event more salient
Stay unchanged, because with no juice there is no reward signal at all
Burst as usual, because the bell has already delivered the anticipated pleasure
questions.explanation_en: Dopamine reports reality minus expectation, not pleasure. Once the cue is learned, the burst shifts to the bell; when juice arrives on schedule, dopamine stays flat because there's no gap; when the expected reward fails, it drops below baseline, as if saying "I was shortchanged."

questions.question: 按漂移扩散模型，人在赶时间时做决定更容易出错，原因是什么？
options: 赶时间会让价值尺失准，大脑把选项的价值标错了
门槛被调低，水位更早撞线，噪声还没被平均掉就下了结论
赶时间时证据本身变弱了，漂移速度下降导致选错
时间压力让基底节的闸门失灵，多个动作同时被放行
questions.explanation: 漂移扩散把决策看成带噪声的证据往门槛爬。证据弱会让决策变慢，但图快出错的根源在门槛：门槛调低就更早撞线，随机抖动还没被平均掉。所以速度和准确率天生互相拽着，这不是性格，是门槛高低在悄悄挪。
questions.question_en: Under the drift-diffusion model, why are decisions made in a hurry more error-prone?
options_en: Rushing throws off the value scale, so the brain prices the options incorrectly
The threshold is lowered, so the level hits the bound sooner and a decision is made before the noise has averaged out
Under time pressure the evidence itself weakens, and a slower drift leads to the wrong choice
Time pressure breaks the basal ganglia's gate, letting several actions through at once
questions.explanation_en: Drift-diffusion treats a decision as noisy evidence climbing toward a bound. Weak evidence makes decisions slower, but hurried errors come from the threshold: a lower bound is hit sooner, before random fluctuations average out. So speed and accuracy pull against each other — not personality, just where the bounds sit.

questions.question: 一个人日子安稳、来日方长，却每天只去那家吃了八回的老店，从不尝试新店。按探索与利用的框架，最贴切的看法是？
options: 他应该完全随机地挑店，因为没有任何策略能解决探索与利用的两难
只选已知最好的选项永远是最理性的，在新店上的每一次探索都只是在浪费机会
只要老店的价值标得足够准，探索就没有必要
安稳、来日方长时多探索更划算，未知本身就该加分；长期只利用是错配
questions.explanation: 没有完美解，但一个关键策略是把不确定本身当加分，并随处境调节旋钮：时间长、赌注低时多探索，压力大、时间紧时收回熟悉选项。问题出在错配，比如长期过度利用会让世界越缩越小。价值标得再准，也绕不过这个两难。
questions.question_en: Someone with a stable life and plenty of time ahead eats every day at the restaurant they've been to eight times, never trying anything new. In the explore-exploit framework, what's the most fitting view?
options_en: They should pick restaurants completely at random, since no strategy can address the explore-exploit dilemma
Always picking the best known option is the most rational choice, and every visit to a new place just wastes an opportunity
As long as the old restaurant's value is estimated accurately enough, exploration is unnecessary
With stability and a long horizon, exploring pays; uncertainty itself deserves a bonus, and only exploiting is a mis-set dial
questions.explanation_en: There's no perfect solution, but a key strategy is to treat uncertainty as a bonus and adjust the dial to circumstances: explore more when time is long and stakes are low, fall back on the familiar under pressure or tight deadlines. The trouble is a mismatch, such as chronic over-exploitation shrinking one's world. Accurate value estimates don't make the dilemma go away.
